newsitem.title: THAILAND: Canada PM arrives in Thailand with trade team.
newsitem.headline: Canada PM arrives in Thailand with trade team.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien arrived in Thailand on Thursday for a four-day visit that will focus mainly on strengthing economic ties between the two nations, officials said.
Chretien and a delegation of 10 provincial premiers and hundreds of businessmen arrived in Bangkok on the last stop of a three-nation Asian tour.
"The main purpose of this visit is to take Thai-Canadian relations into a new high-tech era," a Canadian government official said.

Bilateral agreements between the two nations and business deals worth between C$600 million and C$1.0 billion (US$447.8 million and $746.3 million) are expected to be signed during the visit, officials said.

Canada's Northern Telecom Ltd (Nortel) on Wednesday was awarded a telecommunication contract in Thailand worth about US$200 million by local mobile phone operator Wireless Communication Services Co Ltd.
Nortel will supply digital mobile phone switching and transmission equipment to Wireless Communication under the deal.

Chretien will meet Thai prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Friday. He will give a speech to a business luncheon and later Chretien and the provincial leaders will have an audience with King Bhumibol Adulyadej, the world's longest reigning monarch.
